jobs.description:

For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Tetra Tech Solid Waste West (SWW) is seeking an Environmental Field Technician. We are expanding our team and looking for hardworking and capable individuals. Our technicians receive hands-on practical experience and have a direct impact on our environmental projects. Tetra Tech specializes in a wide variety of consulting, testing, monitoring, and maintenance in the solid waste field. Our project sites offer a unique working environment that allows our technicians to gain experience both on an operational and a regulatory level. The pay scale for this position is $22-$25 an hour, based on qualifications and experience.

Your Role

Ensuring all regulatory objectives and due dates are being met, including the proper collection and documentation of environmental data.
The Operation & Maintenance of Gas Collection & Control System’s (GCCS) on our projects. Including performing Routine & Non-Routine maintenance on GCCS components to ensure or restore proper operation and compliance.
Monitoring and analyzing landfill gas (LFG) and liquids.
Monitoring and maintaining the liquids extraction systems within the GCCS.
Critical thinking and problem solving of complex GCCS issues.
Maintaining records of all fieldwork activities.
Ensure adherence to safety protocols, including confined space entry, PPE usage, and hazard communication standards.
Travel to the job site daily. Site location will vary dependent on need. Travel within 100 miles of McClellan, CA is required.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

High School Diploma and / or 1 year of general working experience.
Ability to learn general gas, soil, and air sampling techniques including applicable environmental and health & safety regulations and regulatory requirements.
Ability to troubleshoot mechanical and electrical systems such as pumps, blowers, and other instrumentation.
Ability to develop a good working knowledge of flame-ionization detectors, photo-ionization detectors, explosive gas detectors, water level detectors, PH/temperature/conductivity meters, LFG analyzers (GEM/Envision) and other typical environmental monitoring equipment.
Light equipment operation, HDPE pipe fusion experience is a plus.
Ability to be familiar with operation and maintenance techniques for landfill gas and landfill fluids collection systems as well as landfill gas data, data processing techniques, and databases.
Ability to create professional business documents (letters, reports, memoranda, etc.)
Complete the OSHA HAZWOPER, 40-hour, environmental health and safety class, and annual 8-hour refresher classes.
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and willingness to travel to field sites.
Walk long distances, up and down steeply sloped landfills and outdoor terrain.
Work in extreme (hot and cold) weather conditions safely.
Lift a minimum of 50 pounds on a non-consistent basis.
Pass a company paid, baseline health physical and drug screening, as required.
A.S. or B.S. Degree in environmental, or other natural science (geology, biology, ecology etc.) is preferred.
Proficient in the use of a PC, specifically Microsoft Office suite of products (Word, Excel, and Outlook).

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. This position will provide technical assistance related to geographic information system data maintenance and development. This includes creating, compiling and maintaining data necessary for internal team request to support the business.

Provide support for fiber optic and HFC network mapping utilizing ArcGIS and ArcFM software.

Demonstrated experience handling multiple priorities, organizing work to meet changing priorities, and working efficiently and effectively under pressure.
Proven customer service with internal teams, with sense of urgency, attention to detail, and ability to handle situations diplomatically and across various levels of the organization.
Strong interactive communication and negotiation skills and an aptitude for problem-solving.

jobs.description:
Solutions Engineer – Optical Solutions

Preferred Location: Santa Clara, California
Location Flexibility: Remote

Overview

Keysight
is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~15,000 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.

Our award-winning
culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.

The Solutions Engineer – Optical Solutions is a highly visible, customer-facing role at the forefront of next-generation optical networking. You'll partner directly with AI data center operators, optical module vendors, and hyperscalers to solve complex engineering challenges and architect innovative optical test and validation solutions that power the next generation of AI infrastructure. As Keysight continues to expand its optical portfolio, you'll play a pivotal role in connecting customer needs with breakthrough technologies, helping shape how the industry's most advanced optical systems are designed, validated, and brought to market.

This position is ideally based in the Santa Clara, California area to enable close collaboration with customers and local teams. However, for exceptional candidates located elsewhere in the United States, remote work may be considered with the expectation of approximately 50% travel to customer sites and Keysight locations as business needs require.

Responsibilities

As a Solutions Engineer – Optical Solutions, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor, partnering with customers to solve complex optical engineering challenges by designing and delivering end-to-end test and validation solutions that integrate Keysight hardware, software, and ecosystem technologies.

You will:
Partner with AI data centers, hyperscalers, optical module vendors, and silicon photonics companies to understand complex system-level challenges and develop customized optical test and validation solutions.
Serve as the technical bridge between customers, Sales, and Keysight's Optical Center of Excellence (COE), helping translate customer requirements into innovative, scalable solutions.
Architect end-to-end optical test solutions spanning:
Component characterization (lasers, modulators, photodiodes)
Module validation (400G, 800G, and emerging 1.6T transceivers)
System-level interoperability, including SerDes, host interfaces, and standards compliance
Design and integrate complete test solutions using optical modulation analyzers, BERTs, oscilloscopes, network analyzers, automation software, tunable lasers, power meters, and other solutions across Keysight's optical portfolio.
Lead technical discovery with customers to identify unique application challenges, qualify technical opportunities, and define the optimal solution approach for high-impact engagements.
Build trusted, long-term relationships with customer engineering teams by providing deep technical expertise throughout solution design, deployment, and validation.
Identify opportunities where custom engineering, software, professional services, or ecosystem partnerships are required to address customer-specific needs.
Collaborate closely with product management, R&D, and cross-functional teams to provide customer insights that support the continued expansion and success of Keysight's optical portfolio.
Stay at the forefront of emerging optical networking technologies, industry standards, and AI infrastructure trends to help customers address next-generation test and measurement challenges.

Qualifications

We're seeking a recognized technical expert who combines deep optical networking expertise with a passion for solving complex customer challenges. The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in optical communications, test and measurement, and customer collaboration, with the ability to translate complex technical requirements into innovative, end-to-end solutions.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering discipline; Master's or Ph.D. preferred.
Typically 10+ years of industry experience developing, testing, or supporting optical communications technologies.
Deep technical expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Silicon photonics and co-packaged optics (CPO)
High-speed optical interconnect technologies, including 112G, 224G, and 448G PAM4
Optical transceivers and interconnect architectures (400G, 800G, and emerging 1.6T)
Industry standards, including IEEE 802.3, OIF-CEI, and emerging AI interconnect standards
Hands-on experience with optical test and measurement technologies, including products such as:
Optical modulation analyzers
Bit Error Rate Testers (BERTs)
High-bandwidth oscilloscopes
Network analyzers
Tunable lasers
Optical power meters
Demonstrated ability to solve complex customer problems by designing and delivering integrated test and validation solutions.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with experience collaborating directly with customer engineering teams and cross-functional technical organizations.
Willingness to travel as needed to support customer engagements (typically 10–25%; up to approximately 50% for exceptional remote candidates).

Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting AI data center operators, hyperscalers, optical module vendors, silicon photonics companies, or other leading optical networking organizations.
Experience developing customized optical test solutions for customer-specific applications.
Familiarity with Keysight optical solutions or comparable optical test and measurement platforms.
Active participation in industry standards organizations or technical conferences (e.g., IEEE, OIF, OFC).

Keysight Technologies Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. About Bobbie

Bobbie makes European-style organic infant formula manufactured end-to-end in the U.S., because we believe every parent deserves to feed their baby with confidence, without judgment and without compromise. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

The Role:

Our capital plan is bigger than our ability to track it. That's the problem you solve.

You'll be the operating system for the manufacturing program — schedules, budgets, purchase orders,

vendors, documentation, change control, and the meeting cadence that keeps two project engineers and a

plant full of stakeholders pointed the same direction. You won't own the engineering. You'll own whether it lands

Support the Program Manager and Project Engineers in planning and executing capital projects from

scope definition through startup

Track project budgets and forecasts against approved capital, and reconcile committed versus actual

Route scope, drawing, and equipment changes through the site change control process so GMP impact

Coordinate contractor onboarding, safety orientation, and GMP rules for anyone working in production

zones

Bridge project work into operations — commissioning support, qualification handoff, operator training, and

documentation turnover

Publish weekly project status and monthly capital review packages for plant and company leadership

A good fit if…

You're the person who notices the long-lead item nobody ordered
You can chase a vendor, a controls integrator, and a shift supervisor in the same hour and keep all three

cooperative

You're organized in a way other people can use, not just a way that works for you
You want to grow into project management and you want reps, not a title

What the Heath plant is actually like

Regulated infant formula facility — every equipment change carries a change control and often a validation

requirement

Active production: projects happen around running lines, which means real constraints on when work can

occur

A growing capital plan with more scope than structure — you're being hired to add the structure
You'll gown in and walk the floor regularly; this isn't a desk-only role

hear

Willingness to gown in and work in a GMP production environment, and to lift up to 60 lbs occasionally

The Honest Picture:

Regulated infant formula facility. FDA inspects. Concrete floors, loud equipment,

continuous production. You gown in every shift — hair net, no jewelry, no nail polish, no fragrances, dedicated

footwear. No phone on the floor. Coordination here means chasing people who are already busy, and the

Work that matters — the projects you land are the ones that add capacity for families who need formula

Don't Assume - We embrace our unique perspectives, withhold judgment, and find beauty in the paths that

Bobbie makes European-style organic infant formula manufactured end-to-end in the U.S., because we believe every parent deserves to feed their baby with confidence, without judgment and without compromise. But Bobbie has never been just a formula company. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

The Role:

Our capital plan is bigger than our ability to track it. That's the problem you solve.

You'll be the operating system for the manufacturing program — schedules, budgets, purchase orders,

vendors, documentation, change control, and the meeting cadence that keeps two project engineers and a

Support the Program Manager and Project Engineers in planning and executing capital projects from

Track project budgets and forecasts against approved capital, and reconcile committed versus actual

Coordinate contractors, vendors, and OEMs on schedule adherence, deliverables, and site requirements
Run the meeting cadence — agendas, notes, action items, and the follow-up that makes them mean

Route scope, drawing, and equipment changes through the site change control process so GMP impact

Coordinate contractor onboarding, safety orientation, and GMP rules for anyone working in production

zones

Bridge project work into operations — commissioning support, qualification handoff, operator training, and

documentation turnover

Publish weekly project status and monthly capital review packages for plant and company leadership

You're the person who notices the long-lead item nobody ordered
You can chase a vendor, a controls integrator, and a shift supervisor in the same hour and keep all three

cooperative

You're organized in a way other people can use, not just a way that works for you
You want to grow into project management and you want reps, not a title

Regulated infant formula facility — every equipment change carries a change control and often a validation

Active production: projects happen around running lines, which means real constraints on when work can

A growing capital plan with more scope than structure — you're being hired to add the structure
